about: The access policy's shared case file (Sprint 28h, S13, D20). The Java AccessCheck and the hook's Rust parser both run these, so the one deliberate duplicate cannot drift. Every path is written with ${home}, ${workspace} (the session's own project), ${sibling} (another project of the same manifest) and ${temp}; each parser binds them to real folders.

cases.why: a file in the project the session works on
a place on neither list is refused
the deny list wins inside an allowed root
a sibling project of the same manifest is not the session's workspace
a relative path is read against the workspace and lands in the sibling
nothing is inferred from a name the policy does not list
a listed place is refused whatever its file is called
a sentence is one quoted word, not a path
a field that is not a path names nothing
a call that opens the file names it
the word after a redirection is a place
a path after --flag= is a place
the home spellings are one boundary, not several
the same place under its shell spelling
the agent's own guard registration is on the deny list
the rest of the agent-config directory stays reachable
a place the policy declares by name
a call that names no place is not this rule's business
